slides.title: Buy now, pay later: the catch
slides.sub: It splits a purchase into smaller payments. Know the risks before you tap.

slides.heading: How it works
body: Pay-in-four splits a purchase into four equal payments over six weeks. Example: $100 becomes $25 today and $25 every two weeks.
No extra interest or fees if you pay on time. Adobe expects $21.3 billion in BNPL spending online this holiday season.
slides.source: Federal Reserve, Aug. 2026; Adobe forecast, Sept. 2026

slides.heading: Who uses it
body: In 2025, 16% of U.S. adults used BNPL. Among adults 18 to 29, it was 22%.
29% of users said it was the only way they could afford the purchase.

slides.heading: The catch
body: 26% of BNPL users paid late at least once in 2025. For users 18 to 29, it was 32%.
17% of all users were charged extra for paying late.

slides.takeaway: If you can't afford it in one payment, think twice before splitting it into four.

posts.caption:
Buy now, pay later (BNPL) splits a purchase into smaller payments. The most common version is pay-in-four: four equal payments over six weeks, with no extra interest or fees if you pay on time. Adobe expects $21.3 billion in BNPL spending online this holiday season.

In 2025, 16% of U.S. adults used it, including 22% of adults 18 to 29. And 29% of users said it was the only way they could afford the purchase.

The catch: 26% of BNPL users paid late at least once, and 32% of users 18 to 29 did. 17% of all users were charged extra for paying late.

Data: Federal Reserve, Economic Well-Being of U.S. Households in 2025 (May 2026) and Consumer & Community Context (Aug. 2026); Adobe holiday forecast (Sept. 28, 2026).
